Neither AMC nor Ford has shown a clear expression of Congressional intent that the vehicles with the characteristics they described, making them suitable for off-road operation, should be exempt from fuel economy standards established under the Title. Indeed, as has been demonstrated, the intent of Congress would have those vehicles subject to the Title.

The agency realizes that the term "primarily", as used in the definition of passenger automobile in section 501(2) ("manufactured primarily for use in the transportation of not more than 10 individuals") is given a different meaning than when it is used in section 501(1) ("manufactured primarily for use on the public streets, roads and highways"). However, the agency believes that Congress did not intend that the word be used in the same sense in those two definitional sections. As discussed above, the use of the term "primarily" in the definition of "automobile" must be considered against a legislative backdrop of other statutes using the identical phrase, and the remedial purposes of Title V justifying a broad interpretation of those definitions which delineate the scope of its applicability.
